subject: gk
question: The Simon Commission, appointed in 1927, was criticized in India because:

options.text: It did not include any Indian members
It recommended the withdrawal of British rule from India
It recommended constitutional reforms for India
It proposed to divide India into two separate countries

solution:
The correct answer is __**It did not include any Indian members**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the time of introducing the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms in 1919, the British Government declared that a commission would be sent to India after ten years.
 
• To examine the effects and operations of the constitutional reforms and to suggest more reforms for India.
 
• 1919 Montegue-Chelmsford Act could not achieve much and the Simon Commission was appointed.
 
• The Simon Report was met with disappointment and condemnation throughout India.
 
• The Simon Commission was dispatched to India in 1928 to review the Government of India Act 1919.
 
• The Commission, appointed by Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin, did not include any Indian delegates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian National Congress and a faction of the Muslim League, led by Mohammed Ali Jinnah, decided to boycott the Commission.
 
• Upon arrival in Bombay on 3 February 1928, the Commission was met by protests.
 
• In London, the London Branch of the Indian National Congress planned a demonstration upon the return of the Commission.
 
• Indian National Congress mistrusted the findings of the Commission and the Congress boycotted the Report.
 
• The commission arrived in** British India **in **1928 **to study constitutional reform in Britain's largest and most important possession.
 
• One of its members was the future leader of the **Labor Party** Clement Attlee, who became committed to self-government for India.
 
• It was necessary to thwart the increasing prominence of the **Swaraj Party.**
